newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sale of stake in Brazil's Cemig suspended.
newsitem.headline: Sale of stake in Brazil's Cemig suspended.

text.p: Minas Gerais state suspended the sale of a 33-percent stake in its Cemig power firm after federal officials decided not to extend the deadline for the state's repayment of a loan, a company official said.
"We wanted to have the sale in the first half of January. Now we have to wait and see what the National Development Bank (BNDES) decides to do," said Luiz Fernando Rolla, a Cemig financial adviser.
Rolla said the stake of Cemig ordinary shares was used to back 430 million reais in debentures convertible to shares, which was issued early this year to the BNDES to a secure a loan.
The first tranche was due October 31 and the state had asked for an extension of that deadline so it could sell the shares first but the bank has decided not to extend that deadline, he said.
"The state doesn't have the money to repay the loan," he added.
The company notified Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) earlier this week that the state had suspended its sale of Cemig ordinary shares, he added.
State officials expected the sale would garner some $1 billion from the sale of the Cemig stake to a strategic foreign partner.
The BNDES' decision means the Cemig shares will now be transferred to the federal development bank, which must decided if or when it wants to offer them to the market.
Rolla said that, if BNDES decides to sell off the stake, it would have to split the sale price with the state. "So they both end up losing money," he said.
Officlals at the bank, which is in charge of Brazil's federal privatization drive, could not immediately be reached for comment.
Minas Gerais state had expected this month to publish bid specifications, including auction date, base price, sale model and other details of the planned selloff.
The state holds 84 percent of Cemig ordinary, or voting common shares and state lawmakers earlier this year approved the sale of a 33 percent stake to a strategic partner with power sector expertise.
Several foreign firms had expressed interest in Cemig, formally called Companhia Energetica de Minas Gerais, including Chile's Enersis.
Enersis and its Chilectra distribution unit in November bought Rio de Janeiro state power firm Cerj for 605.3 million reais, some 30 percent above the base price.

Other firms which eyed the one-third chunk of Cemig include Southern Electric, Enron Corp, Ontario Hydro and Hydro Quebec of Canada, EDF of France and EDP of Portugal. ((--James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5413))
